description:
The `# Forcing a specific CPU path` section of the feasibility harness backend module states that `permanent_bipedal3` dispatches internally to `permanent_bipedal3_singleword_simd` when the `simd` feature is active and AVX2 is detected at runtime, and justifies calling the single-word entry points directly on that basis.

That is false at HEAD. `permanent_bipedal3` (crates/gf2-algebra/src/permanent/bipedal3.rs:178-197) branches only on `n`: `n <= 63` selects `permanent_bipedal3_singleword`, otherwise the multiword path. `permanent_bipedal3_singleword` performs no SIMD dispatch of its own, and `permanent_bipedal3_singleword_simd` takes an explicit `fns` argument rather than being reached by runtime detection.

The harness code is correct — it imports `permanent_bipedal3_singleword` directly. Only the prose justifying that choice is wrong, which makes it a staleness defect under `@/inv/single-source-prose`. A reader trusting it would believe the study measured a runtime-dispatched path.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: The module documentation at dev/research/permanent-sampling-feas/src/backend.rs states what `permanent_bipedal3` actually does at the revision the text describes, and the stated reason for calling the single-word entry points directly is one that holds.

## Notes

Surfaced by the epic-b8206228 execution lead while tracing kernel selection for 032cc754.
title: Feasibility harness backend docs claim a SIMD dispatch permanent_bipedal3 does not do
